findings.title: Double-checked locking is missing the second check inside the write lock
findings.body: After the fast path with the read lock fails, the function takes the write lock but never re-reads `entryPointAssetsCache`. If N goroutines reach this point concurrently at startup (the common case, since the cache is cold while the first requests arrive), each one in turn will acquire the write lock and redo the full manifest load (file read + JSON decode, or an HTTP fetch to the CDN) and overwrite the cache, even though the first one already populated it. Re-checking `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after `Lock()` removes this thundering-herd work.

findings.title: A failed load overwrites a previously valid cache with nil
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is executed unconditionally, including when `readWebAssetsFromFile`/`readWebAssetsFromCDN` returned an error and `result == nil`. In that case a previously successfully cached value is destroyed and the function returns `nil, err`, so every subsequent call must retry the load and callers that don't check the error can get a nil pointer. The assignment should only happen when `err == nil && result != nil`.

findings.title: Blocking I/O performed while holding the write lock
findings.body: The file read and the (currently dead, but still reachable) CDN HTTP request at lines 54-67 are executed while the exclusive `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` is held, so all other callers of `GetWebAssets` — including those that would be served from cache in dev mode or during cache refreshes — block on network/disk latency. Loading outside the lock and only taking the write lock to publish the result would avoid serializing request handling on I/O.

findings.title: No test covering the concurrent access being fixed
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the `entryPointAssetsCache` global but adds no test. A simple test that calls `GetWebAssets` from multiple goroutines (which fails under `-race` before the fix) would prevent the race from being reintroduced, e.g. by a future refactor that drops the mutex.
